task.description: HARD GATE. Read test/specs/REQ-050.md and the test source files independently -- do not trust TEST-DESIGNER's own summary. Per WF-02 Step 3b's checklist: for each of the 9 acceptance criteria, verify at least one runnable test targets it (not @tag :skip without a passing counterpart); no 'TODO: implement test' left in the spec; test fixtures use per-test-unique data where relevant (this is pure in-memory code, so mainly check no shared mutable state across tests); tests are self-sufficient (don't depend on other tests running first); no hardcoded secrets/connection strings. Also specifically check: are the two describe/test name strings TEST-DESIGNER wrote comfortably under 200 chars combined (this project hit ExUnit's 255-char hard compile limit 3 times already this session -- see docs/anti-patterns.md's newest entry)? FAIL immediately on any check failure.
acceptance_criteria: a gateway whose second declared edge is the first to evaluate true routes the token down that edge, not the first or third -- an explicit ordering test, not a single-edge case

a gateway with a default edge declared FIRST and two non-default edges that both evaluate false routes the token down the default edge, proving the default is evaluated last regardless of declared position

a condition expression that raises a runtime error (undefined variable or type mismatch) is treated as false and evaluation continues to the next edge, rather than transitioning the instance to ERROR -- an explicit test distinguishing this from the no-match case
a gateway where no condition matches and no default edge exists transitions the instance to ERROR with a structured reason naming the gateway node_id AND the conditions that were evaluated
exactly one outgoing edge is followed in every passing case, asserted directly rather than inferred

a condition using an unsupported CEL feature (a macro, a type-conversion function, a collection function, or the ternary operator) evaluates to false via the catch-false rule rather than raising or erroring the instance, matching hasCelUnsupportedFeatures()'s boundary -- at least two such expressions tested explicitly

the CEL-to-expr translation is tested directly on each of its four documented rewrites (variables. prefix stripped, && -> and, || -> or, ! -> not with != passing through unchanged), rather than only end-to-end through gateway evaluation

the evaluator performs zero I/O and is deterministic, confirmed by inspection of its call graph and stated in the moduledoc, which cites src/engine/transition.zig's evaluateGatewayCondition() and src/expr/ as the ported reference and records which subset of the expression surface landed
the two pre-existing tests asserting the old stub error are updated to the new real-dispatch behavior, not left failing

result.summary: AC coverage itself is solid and independently verified: AC1 transition_test.exs:338-357 (2nd-edge-wins), AC2 :359-376 (default-first-declared, evaluated-last), AC3 :378-410 (undefined-var + type-mismatch both fall through), AC4 :446-475 (structured {:error,{:no_matching_edge,node_id,evaluated_conditions}} incl. zero-edge case), AC5 asserted inline via `new_state.tokens == [...]` list equality in every AC1-AC3 passing case, AC6 :412-444 (macro-call has(...) + ternary, both catch-false) plus expr_test.exs:65-96 (6 unsupported-feature examples incl. macro/type-conv/collection-fn/in/ternary/string-literal-false-positive-guard), AC7 expr_test.exs:20-58 (4 rewrite rules each with a dedicated describe+test, plus the != non-corruption carve-out), AC8 expr_test.exs:204-221 (grep-based purity check against expr.ex source, doc-block/comment stripped first) + :223-239 (repeated-call determinism) + moduledoc lib/letflow/engine/expr.ex:2-25 citing transition.zig's evaluateGatewayCondition() and src/expr/ and recording the ported subset, AC9 transition_test.exs (old :EXCLUSIVE_GATEWAY :gateway_not_yet_implemented stub fully replaced by the AC1-AC6 real-dispatch describe blocks; only :PARALLEL_GATEWAY, a different node type, still uses the stub error at line 482-491, correctly) and variable_merge_test.exs:283-306 (AC5 composed-dispatch test updated to {:error,{:no_matching_edge,"gw",[]}}). No @tag :skip, no 'TODO: implement test' anywhere in the 3 test files or the spec. No shared mutable state: transition_test.exs's @node_id_pool/@token_id_pool/@ghost_node_id/@ghost_token_id module attributes are read-only generator inputs consumed fresh per StreamData run, not accumulators; every test builds its own local fixtures via the private node/edge/graph/token/instance_state builders, no cross-test dependency, all async: true. No hardcoded secrets/connection strings (pure in-memory fixtures only). FAIL: the handoff's own explicit additional check -- describe+test name length -- is violated. Computing 'test ' <> describe <> ' ' <> test_name for every describe/test pair in the 3 files, at least 4 pairs land well over the 200-char 'comfortably under' bar the handoff and docs/anti-patterns.md's newest entry set: variable_merge_test.exs:283 (describe 'merge/3 -- immediate visibility to a later evaluation step in the same completion (acceptance criterion 5)' + test 'the composed InstanceState carrying the merged variables is itself accepted by Transition.transition/3 in the same call sequence' = 240 chars full internal identifier), variable_merge_test.exs:267 (234 combined / ~240 full), transition_test.exs:294 (232 combined, :END multi-token case), transition_test.exs:504 (216 combined, SERVICE_TASK/TIMER/SUB_PROCESS catch-all). These are still under ExUnit's hard 255-char SystemLimitError ceiling (so mix test would likely still compile), but they are not 'comfortably under 200' as the handoff explicitly requires, and several more pairs sit in the 170-210 range with no margin. Per the task's 'FAIL immediately on any check failure' instruction, this is a FAIL despite full AC coverage otherwise being sound.
